title.narrative: Maternal and Child Health and Nutrition Services Support Project

description.narrative: The development objective of the Maternal and Child Health (MCH) and Nutrition Services Support Project for Togo is to increase utilization of selected MCH and nutrition services for pregnant women and children. The project has two components. The first component is improved utilization of malaria and nutrition services to address malaria in pregnancy through the provision of intermittent preventive treatment for malaria in pregnancy (IPTp) with sulfodoxinepyrimethamine (SP) and free long-lasting insecticide nets (LLINs), to pregnant women attending antenatal care (ANC). It has following two sub-components: (i) support for: (a) malaria control in pregnancy through provision of LLINs and SPs as part of the basic package of ANC services; (b) community-based diagnosis and treatment of malaria; and (c) management, supervision, and behavioral changes to ensure effective utilization; and (ii) community- based nutrition services for pregnant women and young children under five years of age. The second component is strengthening health monitoring and evaluation systems; project management. It has following two sub-components: (i) strengthening the health monitoring and evaluation system, particularly the health management information system (HMIS), including the government's capacity to monitor its MCH programs; and (ii) project coordination and implementation support.
To increase utilization of selected maternal and child health and nutrition services for pregnant women and children.

title.narrative: Percentage of districts where at least 25% of the received of HMIS reports were verified

comment.narrative: <p>Target surpassed. The improved reporting system went along with an effective cascade verification system, built from the primaryhealth care centers to the district, the regional and the central levels. This has allowed  all the health districts to verify at least at least 25% of HIMS reports received.</p>

title.narrative: Number of LLIN distributed to pregnant women during ANC visits (routine distribution of LLIN)

comment.narrative: <p>Target revised in June 2018 because the team realized the original was overly ambitious. 30% against the original target and 73%  against the revised target. This is due to a double effect: (i) the project has not been able to purchase the total number ofplanned LLINs and (ii) some pregnant women have not followed up on their planned ANC  visits to get the LLINs during those visits. </p>

title.narrative: Number of pregnant women receiving antenatal care during a visit to a health care provider (number)

comment.narrative: <p>Revised end-target partially achieved, but 55.6% achievement rate against the original target.</p>

title.narrative: Long-lasting insecticide-treated malaria nets purchased and/or distributed (number)

comment.narrative: <p>Target partially achieved. CAMEG Togo has faced some long procurement delays and despite the corrective actions the PIU has taken, the anticipated number of LLIN planned could not been purchased.</p>

title.narrative: Direct project beneficiairies (number) of which women (percentage

comment.narrative: <p>Target surpassed. However, the project has not been able to report the percentage of women beneficiaries as required in the indicator.</p>

title.narrative: Percentage of household with children under age of two which was visited by CHW to support infant and child nutrition practices in the Centrale and Plateaux regions

comment.narrative: <p>Target surpassed. With the pilot community-Performance Based Financing, CHWs have steadily ensured they provide support on infant and children nutrition practice to households in their respective villages and communities. </p>

title.narrative: Percentage of health facilities submitting standardized HMIS monthly reports within one month of the reporting month (Percentage Custom)

comment.narrative: <p>Target of surpassed. The training both at the central and the districts levels and the equipment primary health care centers have received to inform and update their HMIS reports have helped in ensuring monthly reports are submitted within the deadline (one month after the month of report).</p>

title.narrative: Percentage of suspected malaria cases tested by community health workers using an RDT
Percentage of children under 2 years of age who attend the GMP session at least once during the previous month in the regions (Centrale & Plateaux) supported by the project

comment.narrative: <p>Target surpassed. The pilot Community Performance based Financing has been instrumental in achieving this result.</p>

title.narrative: Proportion of infants 0-5 months (less than 180 days) of age who were exclusively breastfed (Plateaux and Centrale regions)
Basic list of health facilities developed and updated as planned

comment.narrative: <p>Target achieved. This was a  prerequisite to improve the monitoring of the health centers countrywide, and the entry point to improve the Health Management Information System. The later one was very weak prior to the implementation of the project.</p>

title.narrative: Proportion of pregnant women attending at least four antenatal care visits

comment.narrative: <p>Target not achieved.  The difficulties to track pregnant women, the incapacity for households to pay for health services at PHC centers, and also with some CHWs facing a lack of incentive issues at some point during the implementation have resulted in a lower than expected percentage of pregnant women attending at least four antenatal care visits.</p>

title.narrative: Percentage of pregnant women receiving LLINs during ANC visits

comment.narrative: <p>This indicator was fully achieved, and its target surpassed by 13 percentage points.</p>

title.narrative: Percentage of pregnant women who received 3 doses of SP (IPT) during ANC visits

comment.narrative: <p>The target was not achieved. This indicator lagged behind its target by 59 percent. The Malaria Program and the PIU could not implement the corrective actions on the ground to reverse the course on this indicator. </p>
